summary.headline: Castrol India Q2 CY26 revenue rose 25% YoY to INR1,871 crore and EBITDA 41% YoY to INR494 crore, helped by inventory benefits and pricing.
summary.overview: Castrol India reported strong Q2 (April–June 2026) with revenue from operations of INR1,871 crore (+25% YoY, +21% QoQ), EBITDA of INR494 crore (+41% YoY and QoQ) and PAT of INR348 crore (+43% YoY). Growth was described as broad-based across consumer, industrial and institutional businesses, with two price increases in January–June 2026 and some benefit from older, lower-cost inventory. Management said cost inflation from supply disruptions and commodity volatility began to hit late in the quarter and will be more visible in Q3. The company declared an interim dividend of INR6.25 per share.

segments.name: Consumer (B2C, retail/auto care)
segments.commentary: Broad-based volume growth driven by rural operations and urban premiumisation; POWER1 (premium motorcycle) grew ahead of rest of business. Rural business growing at double digits; rural outlets ~45,000.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Growing at high double digits over last couple of years; about 15% of overall business per CFO. Growth from advanced solutions and expanded customer base.

segments.name: Institutional / B2B (OEMs)
segments.commentary: Works with OEMs such as Tata Motors and Maruti; growth tied to OEM volumes. No separate figures disclosed.

guidance_outlook: EBITDA margin management framework remains 21%–24%; pricing actions are set to keep margins within this band.
Commodity and feedstock inflation expected to become more visible in Q3 FY27, with some raw material increases expected to spill over into Q3.
Management says price actions taken so far are sufficient to offset raw material increases from Q2, but will take further pricing if base oil or FX move adversely.
Lubricant industry expected to grow 3%–4%; company aims to grow at about 2x market.
Capex of about INR100 crore per year, roughly half in manufacturing and half in market (dealer/workshop visibility).
Sourcing guidance of ~55% domestic / ~45% imported broadly unchanged, with quarterly tactical variation.
capex_capacity: Annual capex of about INR100 crore, split roughly equally between manufacturing (health, safety, capacity) and in-market investments.
Silvassa plant was shut for a few days in July 2026 due to heavy rain; fully back up with operating levels at Q2 peak per management.
Paharpur and Silvassa plants completed 9 years and 3 years respectively without significant recordable incident.

National footprint of ~160,000 outlets; auto care range in 40,000 outlets; 34,000 independent motorcycle workshops and 16,000 car workshops; 850 Castrol Auto Service (CAS) outlets; 950 rural service express units.
Building capabilities for specialised EV fluids and data-centre cooling fluids; data-centre business not yet material.
demand_pricing: Two price increases taken in January–June 2026 (late Q1 and Q2), in the low double-digit percentage range; pricing aimed at offsetting supply chain volatility and inflation.
Volume growth described as broad-based across consumer and industrial; company declined to disclose absolute volume (million litres) for the quarter, departing from past practice of sharing it.
Competitor reportedly took around 4 price increases between March and July 2026; management said it will not follow competitor pricing blindly and is guided by RM outlook and margin band.
Group III base oil prices elevated, impacted by Middle East crisis.
Inventory: about half of raw materials bought locally and half from international suppliers; company says it runs lean inventory and that Q2 benefited from older, cheaper inventory being consumed.
E20 fuel: most passenger car brands already compliant; impact on lubricants seen as limited to engine-level fuel-choice issues.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline for the open offer linked to the BP/Stonepeak Castrol global divestment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the deal is progressing but is large and multi-country; open offer timing depends on deal closure, after which SEBI and shareholder notifications and prescribed timelines apply. No timeline given.

qa_highlights.question: Volume vs pricing split and Silvassa flood impact?
qa_highlights.answer: Volume growth is broad-based but no specific figures given; price increases were in low double digits. Silvassa plant was halted briefly in July for safety and is now at peak operating levels, with no impact.

qa_highlights.question: Was there an inventory gain in Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said older inventory bought at softer prices was consumed in the quarter, benefiting margins; it declined to quantify and said profitability grew healthily even excluding this.

qa_highlights.question: Dividend policy?
qa_highlights.answer: No fixed payout percentage; dividend yield usually around 5% including interim and final; special dividends given occasionally. Interim window was advanced this year. Past three years' payout has been in the 80%–90% range per the questioner, which management did not confirm as policy.

qa_highlights.question: Why are price hikes not enough to offset Q3 raw material cost, given diesel prices fell after June?
qa_highlights.answer: Pricing was modelled on inventory and FX scenarios for Q2 and H2; current pricing is seen as broadly reflecting Q3 costs, but the environment is volatile and further price action is possible. Structural cost reductions are also underway.

qa_highlights.question: OCI loss of ~INR66 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a fair-value revaluation of the Ki Mobility investment made about 4 years ago, using listed comparable companies, reviewed every six months; expected to move up and down with peers.

risks_watch: Commodity and base oil (Group III) cost inflation expected to hit Q3 margins more visibly; margin band 21%–24%.
Foreign exchange movements affecting input costs.
Possible volume trade-off or downtrading from the price increases, especially with competitor pricing reportedly higher.
Dependence on Silvassa plant and monsoon/weather disruptions.
Pending BP/Stonepeak divestment of Castrol global, with open offer timing uncertain.
Lack of volume disclosure reduces visibility into volume vs price split.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's results and the broad-based growth story, but cautious on the outlook, citing inflation, volatility and monsoon conditions. Management was evasive on volume figures, inventory gain quantification, the open offer timeline and data-centre revenue.
key_quotes: And this is in context of a very volatile operating environment marked by supply disruptions and commodity cost inflation.
We, therefore, expect the impact of commodity and feedstock inflation to become more visible in the third quarter.
I think we pride ourselves on a very lean inventory profile.

adds.what: Annual capex of about INR100 crore, roughly half manufacturing (health, safety, capacity) and half in-market; no specific new plant or line with timeline disclo

growth.why: Q2 revenue grew 25% YoY and H1 17% YoY with broad-based volume growth, and management targets about 2x the 3%–4% industry growth, but no revenue guidance number is given, no specific capacity addition is disclosed, and cost inflation is expected to weigh from Q3.
